title: ACFIX: Guiding LLMs with Mined Common RBAC Practices for Context-Aware Repair of Access Control Vulnerabilities in Smart Contracts
structure_gain: Removing the AC Context Graph (ACG, built from interprocedural slicing+PDG+call graph) drops success from 94.92% to 89.83% (-5.09pp) on the same GPT-4 model with RBAC taxonomy and validator held constant (§VII-C Table IV)
stop_detail: Five categories of static grammar checks + def-use chain validation + structural-boundary compatibility checks on generated patches (§VI-B, Eqs 1-7), plus an independent validator-agent semantic check in a multi-agent-debate loop capped at 3 iterations (§VI-C)

title: Harnessing the Power of LLMs in Source Code Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: No raw-source-text baseline is reported; all three evaluated methods (BERT, DistilBERT, LSTM) use the LLVM-IR representation. Against prior tool VulDeeLocator: 98.25% vs. 82.43% accuracy, but method/representation/training pipeline differ simultaneously.
stop_detail: Source code is compiled to LLVM IR; for each function call the callee's IR is spliced into the caller at the call site (interprocedural composition) before tokenization and fine-tuning of BERT/DistilBERT/LSTM (preprocessing/iSeVC construction section).

title: RepoAudit: An Autonomous LLM-Agent for Repository-Level Code Auditing
structure_gain: Ablations, same agent: no-abstraction precision 40.38% (21TP/31FP) and no-validator 51.28% (40TP/38FP) vs full RepoAudit 78.43% (Table 6).
stop_detail: Demand-driven, call-graph-guided exploration produces LLM-derived data-flow facts (u@s -> v@s notation) along feasible paths, cached in an agent memory keyed by (function, value); a validator cross-checks control-flow ordering and path feasibility before reporting (Explorer/Validator sections, Table 6).

title: SecVulEval: Benchmarking LLMs for Real-World C/C++ Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: none reported (no with-context vs without-context detection comparison performed; context is always provided, and its identification accuracy is assessed separately from detection F1)
stop_detail: Multi-agent pipeline (Normalization/Planning/Context/Detection/Validation agents) with tree-sitter symbol extraction for external definitions/types/globals; manual validation of 300 samples defines correctness as exact vulnerable statement plus correct reasoning (§4.1, §5.1)

title: LLMxCPG: Context-Aware Vulnerability Detection Through Code Property Graph-Guided Large Language Models

key_numbers.metric: code size reduction via CPG-based slicing

structure_gain: Appendix C same-model slicing ablation: slice-based vs full-code F1 0.8146 vs 0.6762 (FormAI), 0.7250 vs 0.4875 (PrimeVul), 0.6020 vs 0.5078 (SVEN) — the extractor's claim that these were 'not detailed' was wrong.
stop_detail: Backward taint slicing via Joern's reachableByFlows() grounds the LLM's input in CPG-derived data/control dependencies; three security experts manually audited 50 generated CPGQL queries, Fleiss' kappa 0.6429 (§3.2, §4.3.1)

title: ParaVul: A Parallel Large Language Model and Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: Verification/fusion module reported to outperform LLM-only and RAG-only baselines by 'at least 4% (vs. LLM) and 12% (vs. RAG)' in F1 for single-label detection (Figure 4); exact per-configuration numbers not stated in the accessible text.
stop_detail: Hybrid retrieval (dense embeddings over sliding-window segments + BM25) over a corpus of labeled vulnerable code fragments supplies inherited vulnerability labels that are fused with the SLoRA-fine-tuned LLM's prediction via a meta-learning MLP, rather than being concatenated into the LLM's prompt (retrieval/fusion methodology section).

title: VulnLLM-R: Specialized Reasoning LLM with Agent Scaffold for Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: C/C++ F1, full vs no-reasoning ablation
key_numbers.value: Figure-derived aggregates only: All-data F1 ~0.71->~0.78, OOD-CWE F1 ~0.58->~0.81 with reasoning-chain training (no C/C++ breakdown exists)
15 zero-day vulnerabilities found in actively maintained repos via project-level agent

structure_gain: None representation-specific: the Figure 5 ablation varies reasoning-chain training, not program representation (figure-derived aggregates All ~0.71->0.78, OOD ~0.58->0.81).
stop_detail: Reasoning generation is truncated at a fixed token budget (~8,192 tokens at eval, 32K max) forcing a final answer; the project-level agent scaffold caps tool-use interaction rounds for efficiency (inference / agent scaffold section)

title: LLM-based Vulnerability Detection at Project Scale: An Empirical Study

key_numbers.metric: average recall on known vulnerabilities (LLM-based tools)
suspicious/false discovery rate (SFDR) on real-world projects
key_numbers.value: best tool avg 85.3%, up to 97.0% (RepoAudit, C/C++), 94.4% (IRIS, Java)
up to 225M input / 38M output tokens, ~448 min/project average

structure_gain: No controlled representation ablation; qualitative contrast: IRIS's systematic API enumeration reaches 46.15% recall on CWE-078 vs LLMDFA's LLM-inferred sources/sinks at 0% on the same CWE (Section V-A) -- but model, workflow, and representation all differ simultaneously.
stop_detail: Different tools ground detections differently -- e.g., INFERROI explores paths over the CFG, RepoAudit performs 3-layer interprocedural callee/caller exploration to bound path explosion, IRIS embeds LLM inferences into CodeQL query templates (Introduction, Section V).

title: Taint-Style Vulnerability Detection and Confirmation for Node.js Packages Using LLM Agent Reasoning

key_numbers.metric: overall valid-exploit confirmation rate vs best baseline (Explode.js Pkg mode)
private NodeMedic dataset valid PoC rate vs NodeMedic-FINE
newly crawled npm packages (Wild): validated vulnerabilities found

structure_gain: Paper argues a representation-light agent (raw source + lightweight tooling, no dedicated static/dynamic taint engine) outperforms CPG/taint-provenance-graph-based tools (83.75% vs 43.13% confirmation rate, Table 3) and an LLM+program-analysis hybrid, PoCGen, at lower cost (Table 4) -- i.e. less built-in structure yields better results here, the opposite direction from most representation-gain findings.
stop_detail: A ReAct-style multi-agent pipeline (Finder -> Judge -> Constraints Inferencer -> Exploiter) reasons over raw source retrieved via pattern-based file search, then grounds each finding via oracle-guided PoC execution that checks concrete side effects rather than relying on model self-report (Sections 4.3-4.4).

title: MemRepair: Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Repository-Level Vulnerability Repair

key_numbers.value: Full MemRepair 58.0% vs Loop-only (no memory) 36.0% vs OpenHands baseline 38.5%
58.2% overall (JS 74.7%, Go 53.0%, Python 46.2%) vs SWE-agent(Gemini-2.5-pro) 37.80% / OpenHands(Gemini-2.5-pro) 35.60%

structure_gain: Adding all three memory layers on the same DeepSeek-v3.2 backbone raises SEC-Bench resolution from 36.0% (loop-only, no memory) to 58.0% (full L1+L2+L3), a +22pp gain, with L3 (Refinement-Trajectory) alone contributing most (50.5%) (Table 3).
stop_detail: Agent tools return file content with line numbers, ripgrep-based regex search, and Iter_grep (parses the repository AST to locate definitions/use-sites, ranked by proximity to the error location); History-Fix/Security-Pattern/Refinement-Trajectory memories retrieve prior fixes, defense patterns, and failure trajectories to ground each repair attempt.

title: DREA: Decoupled Reasoning and Exploration Agents for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.value: >93% of tokens offloaded to the lightweight Explorer agent

structure_gain: DREA's on-demand repository exploration raises Pair-Correctness from a function-only baseline (19-26% across three LLMs) to 30-42% with DREA (Table 1).
stop_detail: The lightweight Explorer agent uses read-only repo tools (ls, glob, grep, read_file) to gather Repository Context, Code Evidence, and Security Findings on demand, reporting back to the Planning agent, which forms and refines vulnerability hypotheses (Planner-Explorer architecture section).
